claim: Plasma-surface interaction is bi-directional: plasma particles can modify the surface material through processes such as etching, deposition, chemical reactions, and phase transitions, while the surface can influence the plasma volume through particles emanating from the walls via sputtering, chemical reactions, and secondary electron emission.
falsifier: The bi-directional coupling can be challenged by experimentally isolating plasma-volume effects on a surface and surface-emitted particle effects on the plasma, e.g., through controlled surface materials and plasma diagnostics.

conditions: in plasma processing environments where etching, deposition, chemical reactions, sputtering, or secondary electron emission occur
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported review description of plasma-surface interaction; transfer beyond the described mechanisms and conditions is unestablished.

title: Particles from the plasma–mutual modification of surface mechanism
